title: Dia: the teaser (Arc members first)
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: A teaser built from macro footage of the UI on a real laptop: shallow depth of field isolates one control per shot, and four cards carry the whole message (tomorrow, what, who, when). 18 s.
instrument: The two slow pushes are live-action dolly moves on a physical screen, not a screen camera. Cuts read cleanly.

byEye.zoom: extreme macro: one control (the @-mention menu, a 'Write' chip, a 'Give the times' button) fills the frame; nothing wider
byEye.cards: 4: 'Tomorrow' on black (1.0 s); 'A new browser from The Browser Company' over picture (2.5 s, three shots under it); 'Available first to all Arc members' then 'June 11th' over a café (4.4 s); logo 0.37 s
byEye.cursor: the native pointer, seen through the lens
byEye.sound: an audio track with rhythmic onsets (not listened to)

classify: Live-action teaser with the UI rephotographed on a laptop screen. Conventions: macro inserts, rack focus, white cards over picture, a date reveal.

diagnose.observation: Depth of field does the zoom: one control sharp, the rest blurred to colour.
diagnose.principle: Selective focus as hierarchy: the eye goes to the only sharp thing in frame (Murch's eye-trace).

diagnose.observation: Text lives on a layer above the cuts, not inside a shot.
diagnose.principle: Separating the message track from the picture track lets each keep its own rhythm.

diagnose.observation: Shots shorten into the date reveal.
diagnose.principle: Accelerating rhythm builds anticipation before the payoff.

teaches.text: A card can hold across several picture cuts instead of owning its own shot.
End on a logo card; here a teaser's 0.37 s.

critique.like: The message survives with the sound off: four cards, nine words before the date.
critique.wish: Not one frame shows what Dia does; by design it teases, so it teaches cards and rhythm, not filming a flow.
critique.wonder: Could a reel fake depth of field around the point of interest (a blur falloff outside the focused locator) to get the same hierarchy on real footage?
